title: Airtable Notion Integration: How to Sync Without Code
summary: An airtable notion integration uses a trigger in one app to write records or pages to the other with no code. You'll set it up and test it with real data.
body_markdown:
## Build an Airtable Notion integration


### What people automate between Notion and Airtable


You will probably build one of three automations, because they cover most of what people actually build. A new Notion page creates an[Airtable](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/upload-attachment) record, a new Airtable record creates a Notion page, and an edit to a record updates the matching page.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , which counts **750 integrations** in its open source monorepo, exposes each of these as a trigger plus an action. The third one is where the trouble starts, because it needs a stored ID linking the two items.


Read the table for which app fires, which app receives the write, and which app should own the data in each case.


Take from it that the system of record is always the trigger app in the one-way flows, and that the update flow is the only one where you have to choose deliberately.


Automation Trigger app Action app System of record


New Notion page to Airtable record Notion Airtable Notion


New Airtable record to Notion page Airtable Notion Airtable


Updated record to updated page Airtable Notion Airtable


*Prices and plan limits checked against[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/notion) and[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/airtable) on November 22, 2026.*


Build one flow and test it before adding the next, since each row is one flow.


### Choosing which app is the source of truth


Choose the app where people already edit the data, and let the other app display it. If both apps accept edits to the same field, the flow will overwrite one with the other, and you'll find out when a value you typed this morning reverts.


In the table, the update flow points from Airtable to Notion. That's a decision, not a technical limit: a reverse flow is possible, but running both directions on the same fields gives you two writers and no way to say which one wins.


> If both apps accept edits to the same field, the flow will overwrite one with the other, and you'll find out when a value you typed this morning reverts.


**Keep edits to a field in one app and treat the copy in the other as read-only.**


### Requirements for an Airtable and Notion sync


You need an account in each app on a plan that allows API access, plus a connector that can authenticate to both. The plans we priced are listed by[Airtable Support](https://support.airtable.com/articles/1636857517-how-airtable-collaborators-impact-billing) , per seat per month:


- Notion Plus: $10 to $12, depending on billing term
- Notion Business: $20 to $24
- Airtable Team: $20 to $24
- Airtable Business: $45 to $54


Pair Notion Plus with Airtable Team, the cheapest pairing, and it comes to **$30 to $36 per person each month** . The Business pairing comes to $65 to $78.


Since only the people who touch the flow need API-ready seats, count them before choosing a tier, because Airtable Business alone costs more than the whole Plus-and-Team pairing.


Last, have one real record ready in your source app. A test with a dummy row hides the failures that matter, such as an empty field or a select option that exists in one app and not the other.
